scope: Clamp tolerated endpoint contacts to valid segment parameters, and measure the separate effects of clean tracing, added junctions and removed straight anchors. All final geometry, paper and image checks remain unchanged.

method.contactRule: Preserve the existing epsilon test; clamp each accepted segment parameter to [0,1]. Clamp interpolated curve parameters before Newton refinement as well.
method.ablation: Eight explicitly labelled boundary/junction variants. No known hidden connector or sheet ownership is passed to HiGHS.
method.boundaryDiagnostic: Cubic monotone-interval ray sampling with a 1e-9 mm pixel-centre tie convention; exported-template acceptance remains independent resvg rendering.

limitations: Clean square gallery renderings only; no photograph crop or colour-classification evaluation.
Oracle variants expose exact visible geometry and the reference subdivision, including anchors a photograph may not reveal.
The compact graph is restricted to one known valid routing, not all valid template pairs. Missing reference edges do not prove that another routing is unavailable.
HiGHS is still given unknown sheet ownership; independent exported rendering and the normal geometry/paper checks remain required.
Removing straight anchors is a partial junction ablation: original curved anchors remain.
Projection adds knots to existing traced curves; it cannot move an incorrect boundary, join nearby curves, or repair a missing image feature.
Boundary preprocessing is cached within each case; per-variant preparation timings include only the work performed for that variant.
Boundary diagnostics use cubic monotone-interval intersections and a 1e-9 mm pixel-centre tie convention; final acceptance still uses independently rendered exported SVGs.
